messages:
andrea: heads up — image publish to prod-ecr failed on CI for service 'conductor'. deploy-bot rejected it with a provenance attestation error.

deploy-bot: Publish blocked: PROV_ATTESTATION_MISMATCH (attestation builderID differs). image:  public.ecr.aws/redwood/conductor:latest -> digest sha256:6f9a2b4c...

andrea: Error cropped from CI: `provenance: attestation verification failed: expected builderID=redwood-builder-2026-03-18, got redwood-builder-2026-03-19`

infra-oncall: hmm — same digest but different builderID? that suggests the squash/merge step created identical filesystem layers but metadata differs.

sam: yes — we saw this in the local kaniko runs when build args (BUILD_TIMESTAMP) were removed; squashing can produce same blob digests but the provenance attestation includes builder metadata so it fails.

maria: is the root problem that the image digest collided with a prior build so the attestation is for a different provenance?

sam: exactly. CI produced sha256:6f9a2b4c that already exists in the registry from last week's canary; current build's attestation references a different build-id, so the provenance guard refuses the publish.

andrea: what are options short-term? can we retag or must we rebuild?

sam: retagging the existing pushed artifact won't fix the attestation — attestation ties to metadata in the image's signature bundle. quick fix: re-run build without layer-squash (so builderID will match expected pipeline metadata) or include unique build-arg so blobs differ.

tony: can we bypass provenance guard for this push?

ops-bot: Danger: bypassing provenance guard for prod images is disallowed by policy P-SEC-3.2 unless emergency workaround approved by Security.

release-manager: Not ideal for policy reasons. Ops, do we have capacity to re-run the build and push within the change window?

infra-oncall: CI queue is ~6m. re-triggering build with `--no-squash` should produce different quilt. Doing that now.

andrea: thanks. tagging plan? we want to avoid spamming latest if it might re-create collision.

sam: plan: 1) re-run CI with explicit tag `conductor:2026-03-20-rc3+${GIT_SHA_SHORT}` 2) verify attestation matches with `cosign verify-attestation` 3) promote to prod once deploy-bot accepts.

andrea: please post the cosign output here when done.

infra-oncall: re-run kicked at 1769994388. logs: 
```
> docker build --no-squash -t public.ecr.aws/redwood/conductor:2026-03-20-rc3+abc123 .
> docker push public.ecr.aws/redwood/conductor:2026-03-20-rc3+abc123
Pushed: digest sha256:9c2b7d11...
Attestation created: cosign-attestation-9c2b7d11
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: incoming publish attempt for public.ecr.aws/redwood/conductor:2026-03-20-rc3+abc123

deploy-bot: Publish accepted. provenance attestation verified (builderID=redwood-builder-2026-03-20, run_id=ci-4821).

maria: nice. should we still pin the service manifest to the new digest for clarity?

sam: yes — create a deploy PR that pins image digest rather than `:latest`. avoids accidental rollovers.

andrea: I'll open the PR and include release note blurb: "fix: publish collision avoided by rebuilding without layer-squash; pinned conductor image to digest sha256:9c2b7d11 to ensure provenance traceability."

release-manager: also add a changelog entry about the deploybot rejection and remediation (for compliance audit).

andrea: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/conductor/compare/pin-conductor-image-9c2b7d11 (WIP)

tony: FYI — I'll add a CI lint to disallow `--squash` in prod pipeline by default to prevent recurrence.

andrea: ok, action items:sam -> add build arg guard, tony -> CI policy change, infra-oncall -> confirm cosign attestation in prod registry, release-manager -> add audit note. thanks all :thumbsup:

last infra-oncall: cosign verify-attestation output: `Verified:  public.ecr.aws/redwood/conductor:2026-03-20-rc3+abc123 @ sha256:9c2b7d11 — predicate: {builderID: redwood-builder-2026-03-20, run_id: ci-4821}`

andrea: closing thread — will merge PR after one approval. documented in release notes.
